sourceFitAssessment.learnerTask: Compare full/partial agonism, neutral antagonism and inverse agonism relative to a defined no-agonist baseline and concentration range.
sourceFitAssessment.gap: The functional table and10/100/40/5 arbitrary-unit exercise are strong, but the reader must mentally distinguish a lower maximum from a lower dose and a lower baseline from neutral blockade. A fictional response chart is a direct learning aid.
accuracyGuardrails: Label one invented receptor assay, baseline and measured response; receptor abundance/coupling and toxicity controls stay explicit. No universal compound efficacy, clinical benefit or actual-dose inference.
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: The complete accepted owner combines its functional table, concentration/affinity and constitutive-activity explanation, three-condition fictional response chart, caption and corrected exercise. Full and partial curves rise from baseline 10 toward distinct maxima 100 and 40; the marked low-dose full-agonist point and concentration range make lower dose distinguishable from lower maximum. The separate no-agonist panel contrasts neutral baseline 10 with inverse response toward 5, while the fixed-reference-agonist condition shows neutral blockade approaching the same baseline. Adjacent prose and caption define one invented assay, its measured response and arbitrary concentration units, including the enlarged middle axis and off-axis zero. The corrected exercise explicitly requires receptor-mediated reduction and excludes toxicity, background changes and unnoticed agonist; receptor abundance and coupling remain explicit. This covers the full frozen comparison task and keeps assay efficacy, occupancy, actual clinical dose and patient benefit separate.
